propositions: Directory and first event file creation is not atomic in _prepare_event and batch_stage_and_commit; mkdir occurs outside the write lock before os.replace lands the first event file, creating a window where interruption leaves an empty ticket directory visible to fsck.

fsck reports empty stray ticket directories as both MISSING_CREATE (no event found after dir exists) and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH (worktree strays); these debris signatures cannot be automatically cleaned per bug 043f, so prevention at writer is required.

Staging dir creation is made atomic by building dir and first event together in a dot-prefixed temporary path (.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex>), then publishing via single os.rename under the existing write lock; temp paths are invisible to fsck due to existing dot-prefix exclusion rules.

Same atomic pattern is applied to all dir-then-first-file sites in the store write path: batch_stage_and_commit, inbound_translate._write_event_file, and dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT emission; _rollback_batch removes directories it created once events are gone.

Bounded, best-effort sweep of stale staging directories on writer start removes only .tmp-newticket-* dirs owned by provably-dead pids using host+pid-namespace+process-start-time stamp, respecting 043f boundary by never touching ticket dirs or store data.
